q: Agra has 50 cupola and 30 induction foundries: what does the cluster emit, and where is the saving?
title: Agra foundries: cupola vs induction carbon
short: TERI put Agra's 80 working foundries at 10,310 toe and 77,743 t CO2 in 2017-18, about 90% of it from 85 million kWh of electricity. The 30 induction units make 65% of the castings, so the biggest saving sits in their old SCR furnaces: about 680 kWh a tonne, against 540 for IGBT.
audience: Foundry owners in Rambagh, Nunhai and Foundrynagar, Agra, and their associations

ul: Over 100 foundries once, about 80 working now: 40 micro, 23 small, 15 medium and 2 large.
About 360 t of castings a day, roughly 0.11 million t a year, for DG sets, automotive, air compressors and general engineering.
50 cupola foundries make about 35% of the output; 30 induction foundries make the other 65%.
Most cupolas here burn piped natural gas, 60 to 70 SCM per tonne of molten metal, not coke. The small ones melt once or twice a week.
Electricity, 85 million kWh: 69,700 t CO2 on TERI's factor.
Graphite for the cupola bed, 1,422 t: 4,141 t.
Melting takes about 90% of a cupola unit's energy and 75 to 80% of an induction unit's.

sections.h: Why the induction shops hold the saving
p: About 95% of the 30 induction furnaces are SCR type, roughly a decade old, run without standard operating procedures at around 680 kWh per tonne of metal. An IGBT furnace brings that to about 540, a 15 to 25% cut, and TERI's costing showed a Rs 40 lakh furnace paying back in about 1.1 years at 250 t a month. A lid on the open crucible, which loses 6 to 8% of the energy as radiation, saves up to 3% more and paid back in about 7 months.

sections.h: Before you take the upgrade to a lender
ul: Twelve months of power bills and your monthly melt in tonnes, so kWh per tonne is your own figure, not TERI's average.
The IGBT supplier's quotation with the kWh per tonne it commits to.
A note of whether the old furnace will be scrapped or kept as standby, because a lender will ask.

example.title: Worked example: one 250 t a month induction shop moves to IGBT
lines: Saving: 680 minus 540 = 140 kWh per tonne of metal
CO2 at the FY 2025-26 grid factor: 420,000 x 0.675 = about 284 t a year
If all 30 induction units switched, on their 70,000 t of castings: 140 x 70,000 = 9.8 million kWh, about 6,615 t CO2
example.note: TERI's furnace figures with Senseible's grid factor of 0.675 kg per kWh; TERI's own CO2 figures used an older, higher factor. Metal melted exceeds castings shipped, so the cluster line is a low estimate.

senseible: Upload a year of power bills and gas invoices and Senseible turns them into dated monthly records; divide by the tonnes in your melting log for your own kWh per tonne. Its green loan check then shows what evidence a lender will want before funding an IGBT furnace.
